item.title: Contratto di ricerca: CR 15-2026 IEOMI NA - MITCAN — MITotic Checkpoint and chromosomal instAbility in caNcer (Istituto degli Endotipi in Oncologia, Metabolismo e Immunologia "G. Salvatore" (CNR-IEOMI))
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-10-24 18:00
Institution: Istituto degli Endotipi in Oncologia, Metabolismo e Immunologia "G. Salvatore" (CNR-IEOMI), Napoli
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-10 Biologia cellulare e applicata

The MITCAN project aims to develop anti-cancer drugs targeting the GRASP65–GM130 axis, a pathway crucial for the mitotic spindle and chromosomal stability. The work involves characterizing protein-protein interfaces and analyzing the druggability of binding sites using structural molecular modeling, while also handling incomplete experimental data. To identify modulating molecules, the project will employ virtual screening campaigns (both ligand- and structure-based), drug repurposing studies, pharmacophore modeling, and molecular dynamics simulations. item.title: Contratto di ricerca: Development of nucleic acid molecules aimed at recovering mitochondrial dysfunction in cancer and neurodegenerative diseases. (Univ. CATANIA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-10-22 12:00
Institution: Univ. CATANIA, Catania
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-08 Biologia molecolare

The project aims to develop new therapeutic strategies based on targeting the mitochondrial protein VDAC in tumours and neurodegenerative diseases. The first objective is to interfere with the VDAC-Hexokinase-1 (HK1) complex, which plays a central role in both the mitochondrial dysfunction associated with neurodegeneration and the metabolic advantage and resistance to apoptosis exhibited by cancer cells. To this end, RNA molecules encoding interfering peptides will be developed, including the NHK1 sequence, a patented peptide. The second objective is to reduce VDAC overexpression through the use of lncRNAs or circRNAs derived from VDAC pseudogenes, in particular the VDAC1P8 pseudogene,…

item.title: Contratto di ricerca: The impact of psychedelics on neurodevelopment (Univ. CATANIA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-10-22 12:00
Institution: Univ. CATANIA, Catania
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-11 Farmacologia

This project investigates the reproductive safety, teratological risks, and therapeutic potential of prenatal psilocybin exposure and its interaction with a model of prenatal THC exposure, the main psychoactive component of Cannabis plant. The main objective is to evaluate whether psilocybin induces long-term alterations in maternal care or offspring neurodevelopment, or whether it can mitigate THC-induced cognitive-social deficits by acting on synaptic plasticity and the modulation of the serotonergic and endocannabinoid systems.
